::: {#hero-heading}

I'm William Pearman - at the moment I am a Research Fellow at the University of Auckland, working on host-microbe evolution questions, using simulations. However more broadly I am a molecular ecologist, working on a range of projects from whole genome sequencing and population genomics, eDNA, microbial ecology, and nanopore sequencing of recalcitrant species. 


I did my PhD at the University of Otago, in Dunedin - New Zealand. My PhD focused on seaweed population genomics and microbiome structure - although I dabble in a variety of various other areas. 
## Education 

* University of Otago, Dunedin, New Zealand
    *    PhD in Genetics/Marine Biology | 2023

* Massey University, Auckland, New Zealand
    *    Masters of Natural Science (Distinction) - speciality: Molecular Ecology | 2020
    *    Bachelor of Natural Science - speciality: Molecular Ecology | 2018


## Experience

* Extensive experience in R - data visualization, analysis, eDNA/metabarcoding analysis, and simulation
* Extensive command line bioinformatic experience - genome assembly, variant calling, metagenomic analysis
* Project management
* Scientific publishing


## Service & Outreach

    * Molecular Ecology
    * Molecular Ecology Resources

* Committee Member - University of Auckland Faculty of Science Reserach Fellow Society
* Organizer - University of Auckland MicroGroup
* Invited Speaker to science communication talks, All Saints Church - Birkenhead
